vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: web-collection
Version: 1.1.1

The skill bundle contains a critical shell injection vulnerability via the `--bridge-cmd` parameter in `scripts/collect_and_export_loop.sh`, which executes arbitrary strings using `bash -lc`. The `SKILL.md` instructions explicitly encourage the AI agent to use this parameter with hardcoded local paths (e.g., `/Users/zhym/...`), providing a direct vector for Remote Code Execution (RCE) if the agent is manipulated via prompt injection. While the tool's stated purpose is social media data collection, the capability to execute arbitrary shell commands to 'ensure the bridge' is a high-risk design flaw.

llm.summary: The skill's behavior (collecting via a local browser bridge) matches its description, but the bundled scripts expect and execute local programs/commands (node, curl, nohup + a user-supplied bridge command) while the skill metadata does not declare those dependencies and it contains hard-coded developer paths — this mismatch and the ability to run arbitrary bridge commands are concerning.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description (browser-bridge data collection for Douyin/TikTok/Xiaohongshu) aligns with the included scripts that POST to a local bridge and poll task endpoints. However, the scripts rely on local binaries (node, curl, tail) and assume a bridge server at localhost:19820; the registry metadata declares no required binaries or environment variables. The scripts also reference a hard-coded developer path (/Users/zhym/...) as a default working directory/bridge command, which is unexpected in generic skill metadata.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run the bundled shell scripts. The scripts implement logic to start and wait for a local bridge, and when --ensure-bridge is used they run the exact bridge command via nohup bash -lc "$BRIDGE_CMD". That means the skill will execute arbitrary shell commands provided as the bridge command. The instructions also tell the agent to use the provided bridge command exactly, which grants the agent the ability to run arbitrary local commands if it constructs or is given a bridge-cmd.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install specification (instruction-only with bundled scripts). No external downloads or package installs are requested by the skill metadata, which is lower risk. The included code files are shipped with the skill rather than fetched from external URLs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or primary credential, which is consistent with not requesting secrets. However, the scripts read several environment variables (e.g., WEB_COLLECTION_LOCAL_WORKDIR) and the Node helper reads many environment values when building payloads (PLATFORM, METHOD, KEYWORDS_JSON, etc.). The metadata omission of required runtime binaries (node, curl) is a proportionality/information gap rather than a secret-exfiltration issue.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The scripts may start a background bridge process (nohup ...) and write logs to /tmp/web-collection-bridge.log, so the skill can create a persistent local process and files. The skill metadata does not request always:true and does not modify other skills; the persistence here is limited to starting the bridge process and writing its log, which is expected behavior for a local bridge but should be treated cautiously.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it advertises (drive a local browser-extension bridge and collect/export data), but be cautious before enabling it: 1) The scripts call local programs (node, curl, tail) even though the metadata doesn't list required binaries — make sure those tools are installed and the skill metadata/maintainer confirms them. 2) The --ensure-bridge path runs whatever bridge command you provide with nohup and bash -lc; do not pass an unfamiliar or untrusted bridge-cmd because it will execute arbitrary shell commands on your machine. 3) The bundled defaults reference a developer's absolute path (/Users/zhym/...), change these to safe local paths or run the bridge manually instead of relying on --ensure-bridge. 4) If you plan to let the agent invoke this skill autonomously, prefer starting the bridge yourself (manual), or restrict the bridge-cmd to a vetted script. 5) Review the scripts (they're included) and confirm they only talk to localhost:19820 and do not exfiltrate data to external endpoints you don't expect. If the author can clarify declared dependencies and remove hard-coded developer paths (or document them), my confidence in benign behavior would increase.
